problem: New, from the step3-jobs-fix-4-C1-1 fix. The branch _wait_for_running gained for a settling start call that died reads the record and then probes the settle lock. It calls stop_products on that read. This is the snapshot class S3R-jobs-C2-1 named, and the C2-1 fix closed it only in _held_answer's first branch, which re-reads after the probe. A live start call writes 'running' and then releases the settle lock (its env.started emit sits between the two). If both happen between the waiter's read and its settle probe, the waiter takes the healthy, settling call for a dead one. stop_products(subject) re-reads the record, finds it 'running' under a held lock, and kills the product the first call has just reported. The waiter then takes the lock and starts a second product. D14 says a second start at the same commit returns the first. Before this round the settle-held wait only polled for 'running' and stopped nothing, so the fix introduced this. Probe in a scratch copy: SETTLE_SECONDS 1.0, a second start joining a first start's settle window, and only the settle probe made from _wait_for_running delayed 1.5 s. The first call returned 0 with pid 74936, which was dead afterwards. The second returned 0 with a new pid 75340, and the record named 75340. With the pre-fix env.py the same probe returned the first pid to both calls, and the product stayed alive.
proposed_resolution: Decide on a read made after the settle probe, as _held_answer's first branch does. In _wait_for_running, when a read says 'starting' and the settle lock is then found free, read the record again. If it now says 'running', go round the loop so the running branch answers it or replaces it. Treat the record as a dead settler's only when the second read is still 'starting' with the same nonce as the first. A different nonce means a new start call wrote it, so keep waiting. Add a test to test_env.py that widens the window by delaying the settle probe made from _wait_for_running. With a start in flight at the same commit, it asserts that both calls return the same pid and that the product is alive.

problem: Old code, from the S3R-jobs-C2-1 fix; this round did not touch it. It falls in the work's case list: a start in flight over a stale record with nothing alive. Every case where the record is absent or 'running' now waits for the holder. A stale 'starting' record (the settling call is dead, its orphan is dead, the lock is free) does not. Suppose start Y takes the lock and an overlapping start W reads that record before Y unlinks it. W probes the settle lock and finds it free, because Y has not yet reached _launch. W then assumes that the lock holder is the dead settler's orphan and calls stop_products. But the orphan's group is gone and Y is the holder. stop_products finds nothing it may stop: Y's record is unlinked, or Y holds the settle lock. If it still lists the stale record before Y takes the settle lock, it waits out its 5 s grace on Y's lock. W then gets None, and start()'s single re-probe returns 1, 'the product lock stays held', while Y answers a pid. D14 says W returns Y's product. Probe in a scratch copy: a stale 'starting' record with pid 999999, Y's unlink of it held back until W reached stop_products or _wait_for_running, both starts at the same head commit. W returned 1, 'the product lock stays held', after 0.02 s and after 0.32 s, with the stale record at the head commit and at another commit. The pre-fix env.py gives the same results. The test_env.py case comment (case 5: 'one that has taken the lock but not yet written, record or none - is waited on like a start in flight') claims more than is true. So does commands/env-start.md ('whether the record is absent or still starting'). No test covers a stale 'starting' record under a start in flight.
proposed_resolution: Stop on a 'starting' record only when its orphan is what holds the lock. Send _held_answer's 'starting' snapshot, whether its settle lock is held or free, to _wait_for_running and drop the separate first branch. In _wait_for_running's dead-settler branch (after the re-read of step3-jobs-fix-4-C2-1), call stop_products(subject) and return None only when the record still has the first read's nonce and _group_alive(record['pid']) holds. When the group is gone, the holder is a start in flight (or an escaped holder), so keep waiting: answer its running record at the same commit, replace it at another, take a freed lock, or fail after _STARTING_WAIT. A scratch-copy version of this change (with the C2-1 re-read) passed every test in test_env.py, the C2-1 probe, and this probe at both record commits (W returned Y's pid after 0.42 s). Add tests to test_env.py: a stale 'starting' record (pid 999999) under a start in flight that has yet to unlink it. At the head commit W returns Y's pid. At another commit (env._head split per thread) W returns a new pid, the record names W's commit and Y's product is gone. Both must finish well inside _STARTING_WAIT. Keep test_start_recovers_from_a_start_call_killed_mid_settle and test_start_takes_over_when_the_settling_start_call_dies passing, since there the orphan's group lives and it is stopped. Correct the case comment.
